record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can the three-quasi-particle scattering approach be extended to the N-body quasi-particle case by proving existence of the free channel wave operator and proving absence of weakly localized solutions for initial data in the continuous spectral subspace of the Hamiltonian? The expected difficulty is the need for many new propagation estimates.

evidence.quote: 14.5. N-Quasi-Particles. We have demonstrated that the three quasi-particle case is manageable using the new approach Soffer and Wu (2023b). It is also possible that the proof of the free channel wave operator exists in the N-body case, leaving the task of proving the absence of weakly localized solutions for initial conditions in the Hilbert subspace of the continuous spectrum of the Hamiltonian. This aspect may necessitate the development of numerous new propagation estimates.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an N-body quantum system in $\mathbb{R}^d$ described by a self-adjoint Hamiltonian
$$H = H_0 + \sum_{1\le i<j\le N} V_{ij}(x_i-x_j),$$
acting on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^{dN})$, where $H_0$ is the free kinetic energy and $V_{ij}$ are short- or suitably-decaying pair interactions, formulated in the quasi-particle (cluster) framework in which the asymptotic evolution is described by independent quasi-particle clusters rather than asymptotically free single particles.

Define the free channel wave operator (in the quasi-particle sense) as the strong limit
$$\Omega^{\mathrm{free}}_\pm \psi = \lim_{t\to\pm\infty} e^{itH}\, F_{\mathrm{free}}(t)\, e^{-itH}\psi,$$
where $F_{\mathrm{free}}(t)$ is an appropriate phase-space cutoff isolating the region of configuration space in which all quasi-particle clusters separate ballistically. A state $\psi\in\mathcal{H}_c(H)$ (the continuous spectral subspace of $H$) is called weakly localized if there exists a sequence $t_n\to\infty$ along which $e^{-it_nH}\psi$ remains concentrated, in a suitable time-averaged sense, on a region growing sub-ballistically (e.g., $|x|\le t_n^{1-\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$).

Prove the following two statements for the general N-quasi-particle case:

(a) The free channel wave operator $\Omega^{\mathrm{free}}_\pm$ exists as a strong limit on $\mathcal{H}_c(H)$.

(b) For every initial datum $\psi\in\mathcal{H}_c(H)$, the corresponding solution $e^{-itH}\psi$ has no weakly localized component; equivalently, asymptotically the state decomposes entirely into outgoing quasi-particle clusters.

Establish, in particular, the propagation estimates required to extend the known three-quasi-particle results to arbitrary $N\ge 4$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of extending the new quasi-particle scattering approach (existence of the free channel wave operator and absence of weakly localized states in the continuous spectral subspace) from the three-body case to general N-body quasi-particle systems is identified as an open direction requiring many new propagation estimates. Recent work (2024–2025) by Soffer, Wu and collaborators has continued to develop such estimates in related (bi-Laplacian, time-dependent, one-dimensional) settings, but no published proof for the full N-quasi-particle case has been located.

status_evidence.title: A new paradigm for scattering theory of linear and nonlinear waves: review and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the N-quasi-particle extension as an open problem requiring new propagation estimates.
status_evidence.claim: The N-quasi-particle generalization is stated as open.

status_evidence.title: Decomposition of global solutions of bi-laplacian Nonautonomous Schrödinger equations
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic decomposition of global solutions into a free wave and a weakly localized part via the free channel wave operator construction.
status_evidence.claim: Related free-channel/weakly-localized results have been established in adjacent settings, not for general N-quasi-particle.

status_evidence.title: Weakly localized states of one dimensional Schrödinger equations have localized energy
status_evidence.snippet: Continued study of weakly localized states in one-dimensional Schrödinger equations.
status_evidence.claim: Active follow-up work on weakly localized states, but does not resolve the N-quasi-particle case.
